sources.citation: Franklin, Karl J. 2023. Samberigi (Sau) and Kewa. Language & Linguistics in Melanesia 41: 51-65.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 'SAMBERIGI PHONOLOGY' (pp. 52-53) is a consonant chart (p t k h; prenasalized b d g; m n l r s w y) and a vowel chart (i u e a ae o, all may be nasalized); the rest is a Sau:Kewa comparative wordlist, a -ke/-ki/-nki/-ko suffix rule and sound correspondences. No mention of stress, accent, tone or intonation anywhere in the 16 pages.

sources.citation: Franklin, Karl J. 1975. Comments on Proto-Engan. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 1, 263-275. Pacific Linguistics C-38.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Comparative Engan phonology; Sau listed among Engan languages (p. 263). p. 267: 'There has been no discussion in this section of phonemic tone or vowel length.. Tone often disambiguates present day minimal pairs' (Kewa examples). No Sau stress statement.

sources.citation: Franklin, Karl J. 1973. Appendices. In Franklin (ed.), The linguistic situation in the Gulf District and adjacent areas, 539-592. Pacific Linguistics C-26.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Appendix J.6 'Sau' (p. 591) is a 100-item wordlist with no stress marks and no phonological note; p. 184 legend 'SAU (West Central) Samberigi (Capell 1962); Okani or Tugi (AR 1921-22)'. Silent on stress.

sources.citation: MacDonald, George E. 1973. The Teberan language family. In K. J. Franklin (ed.), The linguistic situation in the Gulf District and adjacent areas, Papua New Guinea, 111-148. Pacific Linguistics C-26. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 3.51 'Phonological Features' p. 131 has short notes 'SAMBERIGI (Sau)' and 'TIRI (Sau)': consonants observed, vowels, t > [r] intervocalically, syllable patterns V CV CVV CVC, prenasalized-stop clusters. Nothing on stress or tone for Samberigi/Tiri (the adjacent Witu note explicitly says Witu 'features phonemic tone, length, stress', so the silence is not an omission of the topic in the chapter).

sources.citation: Franklin, Karl J. 1968. Languages of the Gulf District: a preview. Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 8, 18-44. Pacific Linguistics A-16.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sau mentioned only for classification (West-Central Family), AR vocabularies and village intelligibility notes (pp. 21, 33, 38, notes 13-14). No phonology.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1 languoid page samb1321; Wikipedia 'Samberigi language' stub; SIL catalogue search for ssx (Internet Archive copy); OLAC ssx page; Ethnologue ssx
sources.note: Glottolog lists no descriptive reference for samb1321 (refs: Franklin 1968, 2023; Ethnologue). SIL catalogue for ssx lists only the three audio entries above. Wikipedia stub cites Ethnologue only. OLAC (connection could not be reached by automated download) and Ethnologue (not reachable by automated download) not readable. No phonology anywhere.

sources.citation: Franklin, Karl J. 2013 [audio]. 54 Sau Word List (entry 53867) and 62 Sau [Samberigi] 229-End (entry 53699). SIL Language & Culture Archives.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Recorded elicitation of the Wurm wordlist plus sentence examples; the only primary audio of Sau, from which stress placement could be checked instrumentally. Not online.

sources.citation: Franklin, Karl J. 2013 [recorded c. 1967-1980s]. 82 Samberigi Notes ('Audio of Samberigi Grammar notes', 39 min 48 s). SIL Language & Culture Archives entry 53868.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only item catalogued as a 'grammatical description' of Samberigi; Franklin's spoken field notes might include remarks on stress/tone. Audio only, not online; would need a request to the SIL archives.

sources.citation: Rule, W. Murray. 1977. A comparative study of the Foe, Huli and Pole languages of Papua New Guinea. Oceania Linguistic Monographs 20. Sydney: University of Sydney.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Comparative description of Pole (South Kewa), the language Franklin 2023 pairs with Sau; may contain incidental Sau comparison and Rule's prosodic notes for the area. Not a Sau description; low expectation.

sources.citation: Mosely, Don (UFM/APCM) and Rule, W. Murray. n.d. Unpublished Sau alphabet notes (cited by Franklin 2023 p. 53: 'Mr. Mosely allowed me to see his notes and work on the alphabet that Murray Rule had done').
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Only known missionary orthography work on Sau; an alphabet statement by Rule (who wrote the Foe/Huli/Pole comparative phonology) could mention stress. Whereabouts unknown; possibly in APCM/SIL PNG files.
